newsitem.title: GREECE: RIOPESCA BUYS 80PCT OF TRITON FISHERIES.
newsitem.headline: RIOPESCA BUYS 80PCT OF TRITON FISHERIES.

text.p: Greece's Riopesca Fisheries, a subsidiary of Selonda Aquaculture , acquired a majority 80 percent stake in Triton Fisheries in western Greece for 280 million drachmas, it announced on Tuesday.

"The buyout of Triton falls within the group's strategic plan which aims to secure the western production and distribution route for end-products of fish farming," Riopesca managing director Christos Giannopoulos told a press conference.
He was referring to the commercial channel that links Greece with its European trading partners.
The acquisition will serve as an important hub in the Patras-Trieste commercial channel, targeting penetration of central European markets like Germany and Austria.
The latest buyout comes on the heels of Selonda's recent acquisition of a 40 percent stake in Italy's Marina & Maricolture Alto Adriatico (MMAA) based in Trieste.
Triton, founded in 1989, is located 20 kilometres from the port of Igoumenitsa in western Greece with its productive facilities close to the tourist resorts of the island of Corfu.
The location benefits by a water temperature profile very suitable to fish farming, meaning it can put out end-products in 18-20 months, Giannopoulos said.
"It also happens to be a hub of maritime routes to Italy -- the largest market for aquaculture products," he told reporters.
Triton produced 120 tonnes of fish in 1996, most of it sold to Italy. It had sales of 200 million drachmas and pretax earnings of 20 million.
It has benefited from Riopesca's know-how in the production of fry and a new facility subsidised with 279 million drachmas by the European Union will see completion this year.
It will realise fry output of four million this year and seven million in 1998 with respective production of 200 and 300 tonnes of sea bream and bass.
Triton's projected sales this year will grow to 620 million drachmas and to 1.1 billion in 1998. Profits are seen around 150 million and 300 million drachmas, respectively.

The 25-day farmers blockade in December last year which crippled transport affected Riopesca's sales in the seasonally strong December. The impact was foregone sales of around 200 tonnes, Giannopoulos said.

As a result, Riopesca's fiscal 1996 sales will slip 16 percent to 2.1-2.2 billion drachmas from 2.63 billion a year earlier. Pretax profit will be 800 million drachmas, down 14.4 percent from 935 million in 1995, he said.
The company invested 150 million drachmas in state-of-the art ozone generators, a new technology that cleans waters in its fry production facility.
Selonda chief executive John Stefanis told the conference the European Union's balance of trade in fish products is in deficit.
With total demand amounting to 9.0 million tonnes, EU landings of fish are around six million tonnes of which 1.4 million are exported.
Fish farming is only contributing 400,000 tonnes and the balance is satisfied by imports from other countries -- about 4.0 million tonnes valued at 8.0 billion ecu.

He said that according to Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) projections, world demand for fish for human consumption will rise to 110-120 million tonnes by the year 2010 from 75 million tonnes in 1995.
Supply will range between 70-110 million tonnes with fish farming seen contributing 27-39 million tonnes of fish. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
